mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes Sprinter 208-316 CDI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt OM651 engine for the Sprinter 208-316 CDI costs £2,400-£4,500 supply-only, depending on variant and power output. Supply-and-fit adds £450-£850 labour. Prices vary by variant, engine code, and specialist location across the UK network.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure on a Mercedes Sprinter 208-316 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rattling noise on cold start is the classic warning sign on the OM651 engine. The timing chain tensioner seal can leak oil (REC-005099 recall), causing chain slack and guide wear. If ignored, it can lead to catastrophic engine failure and significant commercial downtime.

mainEntity.name: What causes the OM651 injector seal failure (Black Death) on a Mercedes Sprinter?

acceptedAnswer.text: The original copper injector seat seals harden and crack over time, allowing high-pressure combustion gases to blow past the injector. This rapidly carbonises the injector bore and cylinder head, eventually warping the sealing surface. Early Delphi piezo injectors (pre-2012) are particularly prone to failure.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes Sprinter 208-316 CDI OM651 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM651 is fundamentally a robust and reliable commercial diesel engine - 200,000-300,000 km examples are common. However, it has predictable weak points: timing chain tensioner seal leaks (REC-005099), injector seal blow-by, and EGR cooler cracking. All are manageable with the right maintenance schedule and proactive attention.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes Sprinter 208-316 CDI engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained OM651 engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000 miles before major work. Timing chain tensioner issues typically appear between 60,000-110,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes Sprinter 208-316 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the Sprinter is otherwise in good condition with no structural rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt OM651 costs £2,400-£4,500 - far less than replacing a £4,000-£15,000 vehicle. Commercial operators typically save £15,000-£30,000 versus purchasing a new Sprinter van.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz Sprinter 208/211/313/316 CDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The W906 Sprinter launched in 2006 with the all-new OM651 2.1-litre four-cylinder diesel engine family, replacing older five-cylinder units and establishing the powertrain that would dominate UK commercial van registrations for over a decade. The OM651 was available in three power output classes across the 208-316 CDI range: 95hp for entry-level 208/210 CDI variants, 129hp for the core 213/313 CDI models, and 163hp for the high-output 216/316 CDI variants. Production continued through to 2018 when the VS30 generation introduced the OM654 engine, making the W906 Sprinter and its OM651 engines the most widely replaced commercial van powertrains in the UK.

milestones.description: OM651.950, 2.1L four-cylinder diesel, 80-109hp (208 CDI, 211 CDI, W906 launch)
OM651.950, 2.1L four-cylinder diesel, 95kW/129hp (213 CDI, 313 CDI, W906 launch)
OM651.958, 2.1L four-cylinder diesel, 120kW/163hp (216 CDI, 316 CDI, Euro 5 introduction)

problems.group: OM651 Timing Chain Tensioner Seal Leak
problems.h4: OM651 Timing Chain Tensioner Seal Leak - The Most Critical Sprinter Diesel Failure
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Sprinter 208 CDI, 211 CDI, 313 CDI, 316 CDI (OM651.950, OM651.955, OM651.958, 2006-2018)
problems.rootCause: The seal ring between the timing chain tensioner and the engine may leak oil due to manufacturing tolerances. This allows oil to escape, leading to loss of oil pressure, chain slack, and potential guide rail breakage. A cold-start rattling noise is the classic warning sign. Mercedes issued global recall REC-005099 covering 5,500+ vehicles, with over 100,000 OM651 engines affected worldwide.
